text: “Faith” simply means the refusal to know what is true.
plain: Believing without checking is choosing not to look.

text: Convictions are prisons.
plain: Fixed opinions lock you in and stop you seeing further.

text: Do not allow yourselves to be deceived: great minds are sceptical.
plain: Strong thinkers keep questioning, they do not cling to certainty.

text: Freedom from every kind of conviction belongs to strength, to the ability to open one’s eyes freely.
plain: Being able to see without needing a belief to hide behind is real strength.

text: Great passion makes use of and consumes convictions, it does not submit to them—it knows that it is a sovereign power.
plain: Let your drive use your beliefs. Do not let beliefs run you.

text: To comprehend the limits of reason—this alone is genuine philosophy.
plain: Knowing what you cannot figure out is the start of wisdom.

text: Every inch of truth has been conquered only after a struggle, almost everything to which our heart, our love and our trust in life cleaves, has had to be sacrificed for it Greatness of soul is necessary for this: the service of truth is the hardest of all services.
plain: Facing the truth costs you comforts you love, and it takes a big person to pay.

text: The proof through “happiness,” is a proof of happiness—and nothing else; why in the world should we take it for granted that true judgments cause more pleasure than false ones, and that in accordance with a pre-established harmony, they necessarily bring pleasant feelings in their wake?
plain: Feeling good does not make something true. The truth often feels worse.

text: Life always gets harder towards the summit,—the cold increases, responsibility increases.
plain: The higher you climb, the colder and heavier it gets. That is normal.

text: Everything essential had been discovered to make it possible for work to be begun:—methods, and this cannot be said too often, are the essential thing, also the most difficult thing, while they moreover have to wage the longest war against custom and indolence.
plain: Method is the hard part, and it fights habit and laziness the whole way.

text: The best way of leading mankind by the nose is with morality!
plain: People who want control will wrap it in virtue. Watch for it.

text: When the centre of gravity of life is laid, not in life, but in a beyond—in nonentity,—life is utterly robbed of its balance.
plain: If you live for some later reward instead of this life, you lose your footing now.

text: There are days when I am visited by a feeling blacker than the blackest melancholy—the contempt of man.
plain: Even the sharpest minds have days when they can't stand people.

text: We have all hidden gardens and plantations in us; and by another simile, we are all growing volcanoes, which will have their hours of eruption:—how near or how distant this is, nobody of course knows, not even the good God.
plain: You carry more in you than you know, and it can break out any time.

text: We cannot, to be sure, by any artifice make a rich and richly-flowing virtue out of a poor one, but we can gracefully enough reinterpret its poverty into necessity, so that its aspect no longer gives pain to us, and we do not make any reproachful faces at fate on account of it.
plain: You can't fake having more, but you can make peace with what you have.

text: The poison by which the weaker nature is destroyed is strengthening to the strong individual—and he does not call it poison.
plain: What breaks the weak makes the strong stronger.

text: To be noble—that might then mean, perhaps, to be capable of follies.
plain: Being willing to take a bold, unwise swing is a kind of nobility.

text: If you have a virtue, an actual, perfect virtue (and not merely a kind of impulse towards virtue!)—you are its victim!
plain: A virtue taken to the extreme will eat you alive. Keep balance.

text: The "neighbour" praises unselfishness because he profits by it!
plain: People who praise your sacrifice are usually the ones it benefits.

text: Our strong points sometimes drive us so far forward that we cannot any longer endure our weaknesses, and we perish by them: we also perhaps see this result beforehand, but nevertheless do not want it to be otherwise.
plain: Your strengths can push you past what your weak spots can take.

text: We then become hard towards that which would fain be spared in us, and our pitilessness is also our greatness.
plain: Being hard on your own softness is part of becoming great.

text: The thinker sees in his own actions attempts and questionings to obtain information about something or other; success and failure are answers to him first and foremost.
plain: Treat every try as an experiment. Win or lose, you got an answer.

text: It is common to scare away ennui in every way, just as it is common to labour without pleasure.
plain: Most people run from boredom and work without joy. Neither builds anything.

text: The alteration of the general taste is more important than the alteration of opinions; opinions, with all their proving, refuting, and intellectual masquerade, are merely symptoms of altered taste, and are certainly not what they are still so often claimed to be, the causes of the altered taste.
plain: Culture moves by taste, not by argument.

text: To become satiated with a possession, that is to become satiated with ourselves.
plain: Getting bored of what you own means you are bored of yourself.
